$comment: The pinned upstream sources this package's generated data is built from, following the
pattern of `packages/minecraft/datagen/manifest.json`: every source is a version, a URL
and a hash, so a build is reproducible and an edition bump is an edit to this file plus
a refresh of `pack-hashes.json` beside it.
`utils/fetch/fetch-sources.ts` (the `fetch:sources` script) downloads each source into
`node_modules/.cache/jsprismarine/<source>/<version>/`, verifies the hash before
unpacking, and skips sources whose verified content is already present. For offline
work, `JSP_BDS_PATH`, `JSP_JAVA_JAR_PATH`, `JSP_BEDROCK_SAMPLES_PATH`,
`JSP_VANILLA_MCDOC_PATH`, `JSP_GEYSER_MAPPINGS_PATH` and `JSP_CLOUDBURST_DATA_PATH`
point at local copies and bypass the download.
Hashes for `bds` and `javaServer` are cross-checked against the research notes in
`docs/research/bedrock-data-extraction.md` and `docs/research/java-datapacks.md`. The
two GitHub archive hashes were measured from codeload on 2026-10-24; GitHub does not
promise byte-stable archives, so if one stops matching, re-verify that the commit is
unchanged and record the new archive hash.
The Linux Bedrock Dedicated Server zip, the only publication with features, feature
rules, structures and worldgen. The CDN resets connections from curl's default
User-Agent, so the fetcher sends a browser one. Mojang publishes no checksum beyond
a content-md5 header; the sha256 was measured on download and matches the research
note and the Bedrock-OSS/BDS-Versions sha1 cross-check.
Mojang/bedrock-samples, the plain-JSON publication of the vanilla packs plus the
`metadata/vanilladata_modules` files. Read for the 23 items, the item catalog, the
shapes and the trade tables the BDS zip stores as undocumented binary MCB. Pinned
to the commit of the newest release tag; there is no v1.26.51 tag.
The Java Edition server jar, whose data generator emits the vanilla datapack and the
reports. The URL and sha1 come from the piston-meta 26.3 package, which is Mojang's
own checksum; the sha1 is also the object name in the URL. The sha256 was measured
on download. The jar is kept as a file, not unpacked.
SpyglassMC/vanilla-mcdoc, the MIT mcdoc schema set `@spyglassmc/mcdoc` checks Java
datapack JSON against. Field-level gating with `#[since=]` and `#[until=]` carries
values up to 26.4, so the pinned 26.3 release is covered. Pinned to the main head
resolved on 2026-10-25.
GeyserMC/mappings, the MIT one-way Java to Bedrock mapping tables. Pinned to the
master head resolved on 2026-10-24.
CloudburstMC/Data, the Apache-2.0 dumps of the Bedrock entity, item, block and biome
tables. This replaced a Git submodule: a submodule pins one commit, while `versions`
pins one archive per Bedrock protocol version, so several versions' data coexist.
`utils/fetch/fetch-cloudburst.ts` downloads the selected version into
`node_modules/.cache/jsprismarine/cloudburst-data/v<protocol>/`, verifies the sha256
before unpacking, unpacks only the `extract` names, and links the result to
`src/resources` so every consumer sees one stable path. `--protocol <n>` selects a
version and `JSP_CLOUDBURST_DATA_PATH` points at a local checkout for offline work.
Upstream has no tags, so each pin is a commit on master and the archive hash was
measured from codeload on 2026-10-29. Keep `LICENSE` in `extract`: the dumps are
Apache-2.0 and the license text has to travel with them.
`blocks.json` is only read when `@jsprismarine/blocks` regenerates its tables, but it
is extracted with the rest: it is already inside the same 1.2 MB archive, so leaving
it out would buy no bandwidth and cost an opt-in fetch path.
